Issued at 137 PM CDT Thu Sep 24 2026

Rest of Today - Tonight: Light Rain Moves Into the Region

Increasing precipitation chances are expected into the evening and 
overnight as a mid-level shortwave depicted on GOES-19 water 
vapor imagery and RAP 500mb heights moves north of the region 
this evening. Consequently, much of the CAMs push precipitation 
into portions of southeast MN and northeast IA by late afternoon
and into the evening hours today. Overall, the forcing regime 
with this wave is not overly impressive with much of the forcing
being from mid-level Q-vector convergence leading ahead of the 
wave. Additionally, with a decent amount of dry air in place 
east of this feature from northeasterly flow, thinking that this
system will struggle to precipitate east of the Mississippi 
River. Consequently, the recent HREF has fairly low 
probabilities (10-30%) for rainfall amounts over 0.05" east of 
the Mississippi River. In any case, given the fairly weak 
forcing regime and dry air, probabilities for rainfall amounts 
over 0.25" are very low (under 10% chance) in the recent HREF. 

Friday - Sunday: Staying Mild, Additional Rain Chances

As we head into Friday and the weekend, upper-level ridging will 
build into the region for Friday, which in turn should keep us 
fairly dry during the daytime hours. With some weak southeasterly 
flow in place, may see temperatures nudge up a couple of degrees 
with a few spots topping 70 degrees, however given how weak this 
southerly push is, would not expect too much modification to 
the ambient airmass that has been in place. Regardless, going 
into Saturday we see another shot for rain as a secondary 500mb 
shortwave pushes through the Great Plains and into the Upper 
Midwest. Overall, there seems to be a similar story with this 
system as well as much of the better moisture remains west of 
the Mississippi River with precipitable waters over the one inch
mark in both the NAM/GFS, particularly near I-35. As a result, 
the grand ensemble (GEFS/EC/Canadian ensemble) keeps much of the
higher measurable precipitation probabilities (50-90%) west of 
the Mississippi River with low probabilities (20-50%) east of 
the Mississippi River. In the wake of this system for Sunday, 
deterministic guidance generally favors continued weak 
southeasterly flow, which should allow for some slight warming 
in temperatures. However, given that median high temperatures 
for Sunday remain only in the middle to upper 60s, thinking that
minimal warming will occur. 

Next Week: Mild, Widespread Rain Likely Tuesday

Continued southeasterly surface flow will allow for some ever so 
slight warming into Monday with highs potentially reaching into the 
70s for more of the area. However, dry conditions on Monday will 
give way to increasing probabilities for widespread rainfall on
Tuesday as a longwave trough and associated surface cold front 
will sweep through the local area throughout the day on Tuesday 
with already fairly high probabilities (50-70%) for rainfall 
amounts over 0.25" across much of the area in the grand ensemble
(GEFS/EC/Canadian ensemble). Much of these higher probabilities
are in part due to a strong axis of 850mb moisture transport 
surging north out ahead of this front with anomalous 
precipitable waters as shown in grand ensemble 
(GEFS/EC/Canadian ensemble) with respectable probabilities 
(40-70%) for precipitable waters over 1.5" on Tuesday. So could 
certainly see some healthy rainfall totals from this system, 
particularly if we can get some elevated instability to work its
way into the region. 

Forecast confidence begins to lessen as we head into Wednesday and 
beyond as this moisture fetch will battle against the northwesterly 
cooler and drier air in light of the aforementioned front. The key 
mechanisms for precipitation potential mid-week will be tied to a 
fairly robust upper-level trough ejecting into the south-central 
Great Plains during the second half of the work week. This system 
will likely see a bit of a "boost" in moisture as well given it will 
be ingesting moisture from the remnants of Hurricane Polo in 
the southwest CONUS. As a result, noting a footprint in the 
Shift of Tails of 0 in the EC Extreme Forecast Index QPF for 
Wednesday, suggesting there are a few EC members showing QPF 
reaching the 99th percentile of climatology for this time of 
year. Much too early to deduce if the local area may see 
additional rainfall from this feature as it may remain too our 
south, but something to monitor nevertheless.
